claims.statement: Within the maintained local event population, installed kit sessions preserve explicit, compaction, archive, and legacy feedback signals in one bounded privacy-safe inbox, expose visible lifecycle and repair state, and allow one contained manual promotion into an ordinary opencode-kit OpenSpec proposal.

population.residualSpace: Unemitted human irritations, raw transcripts and arbitrary tool output, unknown secret formats, event populations beyond fixed bounds, automatic scheduling or implementation, cross-machine stores, multi-repository mutation, remote submission, unpinned OpenCode versions, and unrepresented models or prompt histories remain outside the claim.

materialExclusions: Detection of every human irritation or inference from raw transcripts and arbitrary tool payloads
Automatic semantic scoring, batching, scheduling, campaign execution, code fixing, or project-memory promotion
Direct mutation of opencode-kit from a consumer-project session or any multi-repository transaction
Remote issue creation, publication, deployment, release, installation, credentials, or destructive external effects
Eventual disposition of every pending signal before a scheduler or curator increment exists
Complete secret detection, cross-machine synchronization, hosted storage, or compatibility with unpinned OpenCode versions
unknowns: The pinned OpenCode post-compaction event-to-summary identity has not been exercised.
No Kaizen store, plugin tools, compaction capture, archive checkpoint, or triage candidate has been implemented or loaded.
No finite-population member has a current runtime observation.
Signal quality and omission behavior outside maintained synthetic prompts are unobserved.
Required privacy/authorization SDET and fresh evidence-sufficiency challenge have not run.
claims.maximumSupportedClaim: Planning artifacts define the bounded signal, compaction, archive, fallback, triage, privacy, profile, and proposal-root contract; no loaded capture reliability, privacy, cross-project routing, archive-repair, proposal-promotion, or eventual-resolution behavior is currently supported.
